h1:
Chai Nat Temple Day Trip
Thammamun – Luang Pu Suk – Old Sankhaburi
intro: Chai Nat is an old riverside temple town that plenty of people drive straight past without realizing what's here. The classic temple-hopping route runs from Wat Thammamun on its hillside above the river, on to Luang Pu Suk's Wat Pak Khlong Makham Thao, and finishes at the centuries-old temples of old Sankhaburi like Wat Phra Kaeo and Wat Mahathat. We've laid out the timing so you can fit all of it into one easy self-drive day.

blocks.html: If you've got a single day and want to make your Chai Nat temple run count, three stops stand out: the town's own Wat Thammamun Worawihan, the amulet-world favorite Wat Pak Khlong Makham Thao of Luang Pu Suk, and the cluster of centuries-old temples in old Sankhaburi. The three sit in different districts, but they line up along one route if you sequence them well.

This plan starts at Wat Thammamun in Mueang district in the morning, then runs west toward Wat Sing district to pay respects to Luang Pu Suk, and finishes at old Sankhaburi. A private car is by far the easiest way to do it, since there's no direct public transport linking the three temples — but the distances between stops are short, just a few dozen minutes of driving each.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Thammamun – Pak Khlong Makham Thao – Sankhaburi

items.activity: Leave Bangkok on Highway 32 (Asia Highway) heading for Chai Nat
items.note: About 190 km, roughly 2.5–3 hours. If you're already in Chai Nat town, skip this leg and start at Wat Thammamun.

items.activity: Pay respects to Luang Pho Thammachak at Wat Thammamun Worawihan, Mueang district
items.note: An early-Ayutthaya-era temple set on the slope of a hill beside the Chao Phraya. Climb the stairs to the wihan on the rise for a wide river view. Allow about 45 min–1 hr.

items.activity: Drive to Wat Sing district through riverside rice fields
items.note: Wat Thammamun to Wat Pak Khlong Makham Thao is about 25–30 minutes, along a road that follows the Tha Chin River.

items.activity: Lunch before heading into Wat Sing
items.note: Wat Sing district has roadside noodle and made-to-order spots, or you can loop back into town for an evening meal instead.

items.activity: Pay respects to Luang Pu Suk and see the royal-hand murals at Wat Pak Khlong Makham Thao
items.note: Luang Pu Suk's temple — he was the famous monk whose disciples included Prince Chumphon. The ubosot holds wall paintings done by the hand of Prince Chumphon himself. Allow about 1 hour.

items.activity: Drive to Sankhaburi district into the old town of Phraek Si Racha
items.note: Wat Sing to Sankhaburi is about 30–40 minutes — a historic district where several old temples sit in a row.

items.activity: See the old chedi at Wat Phra Kaeo and the carambola-petal prang at Wat Mahathat
items.note: Wat Phra Kaeo has a square Lopburi-style chedi that's 600–700 years old, while Wat Mahathat has a carambola-petal prang in Lopburi style plus Luang Pho Mo. The two temples are close together and easy to walk.

items.activity: Stop at a café or a Chao Phraya riverside spot in town before heading back
items.note: Sit with a coffee and watch the evening light over the river, then start the drive home — or stay a night and add the bird park and the dam the next day.

blocks.title: Timing and dress tips
blocks.html: Temples are open for prayers from morning to evening, but some wihan and ubosot only open during the day or when a monk is around to unlock them. If you specifically want to see the murals inside the ubosot at Wat Pak Khlong Makham Thao, aim for late morning to early afternoon, dress modestly (no shorts or sleeveless tops), and remove your shoes before entering the wihan.

blocks.text: Wat Thammamun Worawihan — the town's temple on the hill

blocks.html: Wat Thammamun Worawihan is one of Chai Nat's old royal temples, set on the slope of Khao Thammamun beside the Chao Phraya River in Mueang district. It's thought to date back to the early Ayutthaya period, around 1577 CE. What draws people here is Luang Pho Thammachak, a standing Buddha image in the calming-the-relatives pose with a dharma wheel on its chest — a blend of late Chiang Saen–early Sukhothai and Ayutthaya styles, regarded as the town's guardian image.

The appeal here is the hill-and-river setting. Climb the stairs to the wihan on the rise and you'll see the Chao Phraya stretching out below — a spot several past kings visited. It's quiet and calm, a good way to start a temple day without rushing.

items: Location — slope of Khao Thammamun by the Chao Phraya, Mueang Chai Nat district, near the town center
Sacred image — Luang Pho Thammachak, a standing Buddha in the calming-the-relatives pose with a dharma wheel on its chest
Time needed — about 45 min–1 hr, including the climb to the wihan for the river view
Good for — temple-goers, fans of old riverside temples, and anyone who likes wide river views

blocks.text: Wat Pak Khlong Makham Thao — Luang Pu Suk and the royal-hand murals

blocks.html: Wat Pak Khlong Makham Thao sits in Makham Thao subdistrict, Wat Sing district, right at the mouth of Khlong Makham Thao where it meets the Tha Chin River. It's the temple of Luang Pu Suk Kesaro (1847–1923), a renowned monk whose disciples included Prince Chumphon Khet Udomsak. Collectors of amulets and sacred objects know this temple well.

The highlight you shouldn't miss is the wall paintings inside the ubosot — murals done by the hand of Prince Chumphon and his retinue, annotated in Khom script. It's rare, historically valuable work. People who come to pray here usually ask for protection from harm and for good fortune.

items.name: Pay respects to Luang Pu Suk
items.blurb: Pay respects at the likeness of Luang Pu Suk, the monk people revere for protection from harm — the main reason most visitors come to this temple.

items.name: See the ubosot murals
items.blurb: Wall paintings by the hand of Prince Chumphon, annotated in Khom script — rare old work. Ask permission first and don't use flash when photographing.

blocks.title: Before you visit the ubosot
blocks.html: The ubosot with the murals isn't always open — at times you'll need a temple staffer or a monk to unlock it. If you're coming specifically to see the paintings, allow time to arrive during the day and ask at the temple first so you don't miss out.

blocks.text: Old Sankhaburi — Wat Phra Kaeo and Wat Mahathat

blocks.html: Sankhaburi district was the ancient town of Phraek Si Racha, an old settlement that predates Ayutthaya. Within Phraek Si Racha subdistrict, several old temples line up in a row. The two most people stop at are Wat Phra Kaeo and Wat Mahathat. Both are around 20-some kilometers from Chai Nat town and sit close to each other, so you can do them back to back in one go.

Wat Phra Kaeo has a handsome square chedi that many rate as one of the region's finest — a Lopburi style blended with late Dvaravati, with high-relief stucco Buddha images on all four sides, around 600–700 years old. In front stands the Luang Pho Chai wihan. Wat Mahathat, meanwhile, stands out for its three carambola-petal prangs in Lopburi style, plus Luang Pho Mo, an old Buddha image that locals make vows to over illness, by tradition.

items.name: Wat Phra Kaeo, Sankhaburi
items.blurb: The highlight is the square chedi in a Lopburi-Dvaravati blend, 600–700 years old, with stucco Buddha images on all four sides. In front is the Luang Pho Chai wihan, which has a carved lintel set behind the Buddha image.
items.meta: Phraek Si Racha subdistrict · about 23 km from town

items.name: Wat Mahathat, Sankhaburi
items.blurb: The companion temple of old Phraek Si Racha, known for its three carambola-petal prangs in Lopburi style and Luang Pho Mo (also called Luang Pho Lak Mueang), an old Buddha image people pray to for health.
items.meta: Phraek Si Racha subdistrict · near Wat Phra Kaeo

items.name: Explore the old town of Phraek Si Racha
items.blurb: Beyond the two main temples, the old town still has historic ruins and small temples scattered around. If you have time to spare, walk or drive a loop to take in the traces of the ancient settlement.
items.meta: Old town area · walkable from here

blocks.text: Where to eat along the temple route

blocks.html: This temple route runs through Mueang, Wat Sing, and Sankhaburi districts, with plenty of roadside and riverside spots to stop at along the way — pick one to match the rhythm of your plan. For lunch, an easy spot near Wat Sing before Wat Pak Khlong Makham Thao works well, and to finish, head back to sit by the Chao Phraya in town.

items.name: Ko Hap Riverside, Chai Nat
items.blurb: A noodle spot on the Chao Phraya in town, known for nam tok pork noodles and yen ta fo. Airy riverside seating — good for lunch or a wind-down before the drive home.

items.name: Khrua Tha Lap
items.blurb: A floating restaurant on the Chao Phraya focused on fresh river fish — tom yum fish, choo chee sheatfish, and the like. Good for a group dinner after the temple run.

items.name: Nuea Tun Nai O
items.blurb: Braised beef noodles in an airy, roomy space, with both beef and pork. A solid quick-meal option while you run from one temple to the next.

items.name: Made-to-order spots near Wat Sing
items.blurb: On the way to Wat Pak Khlong Makham Thao, Wat Sing district has roadside made-to-order and noodle shops — a quick, cheap bite before the temple.

items.name: Chao Phraya riverside café
items.blurb: Cap the day with coffee by the river. There are cafés in town with riverside terraces for the evening light — a nice place to rest before the drive back.

blocks.title: How to sequence it without backtracking
blocks.html: Wat Thammamun is in Mueang district, Wat Pak Khlong Makham Thao is west in Wat Sing district, and Sankhaburi is in another direction. To avoid doubling back, do Thammamun in the morning, Wat Sing around midday, then finish at Sankhaburi in the afternoon — or flip it so Sankhaburi comes first if you're entering town from the south.

faq.q: How many temples can you visit in one day in Chai Nat?
faq.a: You can comfortably hit all three main stops in a single day: Wat Thammamun Worawihan, Luang Pu Suk's Wat Pak Khlong Makham Thao, and the old Sankhaburi temple cluster (Wat Phra Kaeo and Wat Mahathat). Leave a bit early and drive yourself, and you'll even have time for a riverside meal.

faq.q: What is Wat Pak Khlong Makham Thao known for?
faq.a: It's the temple of Luang Pu Suk Kesaro, the famous monk whose disciples included Prince Chumphon. People come to pray for protection from harm, and the ubosot holds rare wall paintings done by the hand of Prince Chumphon. It's in Wat Sing district.

faq.q: Are Wat Phra Kaeo and Wat Mahathat in Sankhaburi far from town?
faq.a: They're in Phraek Si Racha subdistrict, Sankhaburi district, about 20-some kilometers from Chai Nat town — roughly a 30–40 minute drive. The two temples are close together and easy to do back to back. Wat Phra Kaeo stands out for its old chedi, while Wat Mahathat is known for its carambola-petal prang.

faq.q: Do you need a private car for this temple route?
faq.a: A private car is the easiest way, since the three temples are in different districts with no direct public transport linking them. The distances between stops are short, just a few dozen minutes of driving. If you don't have a car, you could hire a local car or taxi by the day instead.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Chai Nat's temples?
faq.a: It's good year-round, but late rainy season to early cool season (October–January) brings comfortable weather, so the climb to the wihan at Wat Thammamun won't be hot. Start early and visit the murals inside the ubosot during the day, since some halls only open at certain hours.
